title: Order Extraction Schema
description: Normalized shape that every incoming order (from email body, PDF, Word, CSV, or Excel) is extracted into. Both the Claude-based extractor (text/PDF/Word) and the programmatic parser (CSV/Excel) must emit this shape. Used as the ground-truth format for Step 1 answer keys and the output contract for Step 2.

customer.description: The buying company as stated on the order. Names/codes are as-written; resolution to a BC customer happens later in verification, not here.

name.description: Company name as written on the order.

customer_po_account.description: Any customer account/vendor number they reference for themselves or for Buckeye, if present.

order_date.description: PO date as stated (ISO 8601 if unambiguous, else verbatim).

freight_terms.description: e.g. 'FOB Origin', 'Prepaid & Add', carrier/account if given.

line_items.description: One entry per ordered line. Empty array if this is an order-related email that contains no line items.

line_no.description: Line number as printed on the PO, if any.

customer_part.description: The part number the customer uses (their PN).

supplier_part.description: Buckeye's / the supplier's part number or SKU, if the customer cited it.

uom.description: Unit of measure as written, e.g. EA, M (thousand), LB, PC.

unit_price.description: Price per UOM as written; null if not stated on the order.

notes.description: Any order-relevant free text (special instructions, packaging, certs required, etc.).

extraction_flags.description: Machine/annotator notes about extraction difficulty for this sample — NOT part of the order itself. e.g. 'price omitted on PO', 'handwritten qty', 'multi-page PDF', 'order spans body + attachment'.
